title: basic-auth web UI entry points: GET /, /version and ui-telemetry map to _allow_authenticated so signed-in non-admins get the UI, not an unprotected-path bypass
answers: Why does a non-admin user see a plain 'Permission denied' 403 at the MLflow root URL instead of the UI?
Why is /version or the UI telemetry route denied for RBAC users who hold MANAGE on the workspace?
Where is the authorization decision for the web UI root and version routes handled in basic-auth?
How do I make a new plain Flask route on app reachable by any signed-in user without skipping login?
body:
Path: The routes that serve the web UI to a signed-in browser: the SPA shell at `/` (also under --static-prefix), `/version` which the UI bundle reads, and the UI telemetry config at the ajax-api ui-telemetry path (GET and POST). They are plain Flask routes on `app`, so they reach the basic-auth fail-closed check through `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_authorized_outside_before_request` and the route-to-validator map in the same module.
Rule: Plain Flask routes on `app` are not returned by `get_endpoints`, so the coverage guard never sees them and no decision is registered; the fail-closed net then denies every non-admin, even with MANAGE on workspace `*`. Map each one to `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_allow_authenticated` in the route map, using the constants from `mlflow/server/auth/routes.py:HOME`, `SERVER_VERSION` and `UI_TELEMETRY`. This keeps `authenticate_request` required and skips only the authorization decision. Do not put them in `_UNPROTECTED_PATH_PREFIXES` or `is_unprotected_route`, since that short-circuits ahead of authentication and drops the login requirement.
Symptom: Non-admin users saw a plain `Permission denied` 403 at the browser root instead of MLflow, and `/version` and the UI telemetry routes were denied the same way; admins were unaffected.
Constraints: Only for UI routes that carry no tenant-scoped data. Left deliberately denied: `/signup` and POST users/create-ui (a maintainer call on gating self-service signup) and GET workspaces/<name> (needs a real permission check, not an exemption). Basic-auth app with fail-closed authorization on.
Applies: Basic-auth authorization for web UI entry points and any new plain Flask route on `app` that signed-in users must reach.
applies: Basic-auth authorization for the web UI entry points (/, /version, ui-telemetry) and any new plain Flask route on app that signed-in users must reach.
says: Signed-in non-admin users get a permission denied error when opening the home page.
Regular team members cannot load the web console despite having valid workspace permissions.
Application version checks and telemetry requests fail with access denied for non-administrators.
Allow authenticated users to view the dashboard without disabling the mandatory login screen.
search: In basic-auth fail-closed authorization, map web UI entry points HOME, SERVER_VERSION, and UI_TELEMETRY to _allow_authenticated in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py so authenticated non-admins can access the UI shell and version endpoints. Because plain Flask app routes are omitted by get_endpoints, unmapped routes default to fail-closed denials for non-admins regardless of workspace permissions. Routes must not be added to _UNPROTECTED_PATH_PREFIXES or is_unprotected_route, which would bypass authenticate_request and eliminate the authentication requirement entirely. This exemption applies exclusively to tenant-agnostic UI entry routes, leaving /signup, users/create-ui, and workspaces/<name> gated.
